title: Telegram Desktop session and cache
whyItMatters: tdata holds the keys that keep the account signed in on this machine, plus the local media cache of chats. A copied tdata folder can be used to read the account.
source: Telegram Desktop (tdesktop) keeps its profile in ~/.local/share/TelegramDesktop/tdata on Linux; see also Arch Wiki Telegram: https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Telegram
notes: tdata is not a readable chat archive but it is the live session. The folder next to it holds downloaded files. The official binary and distro packages use this path; Snap and Flatpak installs have their own trees.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Telegram Desktop, use the export option in the advanced settings if you want a copy of your chats: the tdata session is not readable.
cleanup.signOut: In Telegram Desktop, open Settings, then the menu in the top right corner, and choose Log out, so this computer stops using the account.
steps: Quit Telegram Desktop from its tray icon.
Uninstall Telegram from the App Center if you are removing the app itself.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Ends the session and deletes the local media cache and message database on this computer. Chats stay in your Telegram account.
cleanup.source: Telegram, How do I log out? (Telegram FAQ): https://telegram.org/faq#q-how-do-i-log-out
